summary: Each turn you roll six dice Yahtzee-style, re-rolling to chase claws (attack), hearts (heal), energy, or victory points, while whoever is inside Tokyo takes damage from everyone else's attacks but can't heal. It's a fast, loud, push-your-luck brawl where you're constantly deciding whether to stay in the punishing but point-rich city or retreat to safety.
praised: extremely easy to teach and fast to play
fun monster theme and card powers
criticised: heavy luck can make outcomes feel arbitrary
player elimination can leave people sitting out
little strategic depth beyond dice math
runaway leader problem if someone gets a strong card engine

interaction.kind: direct dice-rolled attacks that damage every other player and forced occupation of a contested space
interaction.detail: Attack results hit all opponents (or the sole occupant of Tokyo) simultaneously, and staying in or entering Tokyo is a constant tug-of-war since it earns points but exposes you to everyone's attacks. There is essentially no private board — health, position, and card purchases are all shared pressure points aimed squarely at other players.
interaction.said: widely called 'take-that', 'mean', and 'a brawl' — reviewers note 'you can't just turtle in your corner, someone will drag you into Tokyo and beat on you'

scoring.how_you_win: Roll dice to collect victory points, energy (to buy power cards), and attacks; you win by reaching 20 victory points or by being the last monster with health remaining after eliminating all others.
scoring.score_note: often ends earlier by elimination instead of reaching 20
